newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Natl Bank unhappy with share rise.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Natl Bank unhappy with share rise.

text.p: Belgian National Bank (BNB) Governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Monday he was unhappy with the recent steep rise in the central bank's share price.

"It's speculation. It's not welcome," Verplaetse told the bank's annual shareholders meeting. "We don't like that and we can ask ourselves if this (speculation) has its place in a forward market. I have my doubts."

But he declined to say whether he thought the share should be de-listed. "I have the impression that until January everything was good and what has happened since is madness, but I do not have any judgement to make," Verplaetse said.

The share has rocketed this year on rumours, denied by the government, that the state would buy back the 200,000 shares, or 50 percent, of the bank's capital still in public hands to make the bank fully independent for European monetary union.

In early afternoon trade on Monday the share was trading at around 58,500 francs, up 23 percent from 47,500 francs at the end of 1996. At one stage before the government denial the share hit 65,000 francs.
Verplaetse said the central bank's status as a public limited company was a historical anachronism, dating from its foundation in 1850, but there were no plans to change it.

"If we created a central bank tomorrow it would not have private shareholders...but what we have works well. I have never heard a minister or Prime Minister say we have to change it," Verplaetse added.

Verplaetse told the assembly that plans to bring the Belgian central bank's statutes into line with the Maastricht Treaty had been accepted and even welcomed by other European central banks meeting at the European Monetary Institute (EMI) in Frankfurt.
He told shareholders, however, that their say over interest rates or note issuance, and hence the bank's profit, was and would remain "zero."
